end.summary:
- Practised making one mark for each object; some matches were right, but the method was not steady yet.
- Practised matching marks back to objects; easy questions were right, with a new-situation explanation still to check.
- Practised explaining why one-to-one matching works without number names; the explanation was not steady yet.
- Parth said they make marks quickly and may make two marks for one cow, causing marks to be missed or repeated; this mix-up was not corrected by the end.
end.parentNote: Parth practised tracking objects by linking one mark to each object, then matching the marks back to check for missing or extra objects. A useful self-observation was that making marks quickly can lead to two marks for one cow, but this mix-up was still present at the end. At home, try a short game with buttons or toys: have Parth touch one object while making exactly one matching mark, then explain what an unmatched mark means.
